difficulty: medium - different domain (legal), no literal template phrases, still fairly clearly 'mere preference, no evidence'
medium - different domain (medical), 3 hypotheses not 2, exclusion phrased as 'ruled out' not 'formally excludes', but full exclusion to 1 survivor
hard - the exact failure mode from run 3, but in a totally different domain/vocabulary, no explicit branch count stated as a digit, no 'formally excludes' phrase at all
medium-hard - scientific domain, weak/inconclusive evidence framed very differently from training ('too small to be significant' instead of 'does NOT formally exclude')
medium - strong falsifying evidence, 2 branches, different vocabulary ('flatly incompatible' / 'definitive control experiment')
hard - 5 branches (never seen at training, which only went up to 4), implicit count (never stated as a digit), no discriminator event at all
hard - 5 branches (unseen scale), full exclusion down to exactly 1 survivor, entirely different vocabulary ('definitively cleared', 'conclusively confirmed')
medium - repeated-agreement-without-new-evidence pattern, but framed as a seminar discussion, no template vocabulary at all

very hard - genuinely ambiguous/borderline case requiring judgment about what counts as 'formal' exclusion (unverified witness = not yet formal), designed to probe real reasoning depth, not a training pattern at all

hard - two SEPARATE strong exclusion events (not one event excluding two at once), 4 branches, 2 survivors remain -- tests whether the model can aggregate two distinct falsification events and still correctly conclude PRESERVE since 2 branches survive
